limitations: The deployed contract (wasm sha256 9376a482c740711803ce30b708221823721fdaef8e24196ca5b78976f8f9410c, byte-identical to the reviewed repo build) surfaces every failing assert/expect path as 'WebAssembly trap: An `unreachable` opcode was executed.' instead of the ABI assert strings; Rust panics compiled with panic=abort become wasm `unreachable` traps unless the panic goes through the env::panic_str host path. Onchain rejection semantics are unaffected: failing action receipts revert all state, verified by the unchanged cycle/proposal-link state after every control.

Template 0 period 1 is contractually not due until 2026-11-12T20:23:03Z (start_at_ns 1793910183011867400 + 604800000000000 interval); materialize_cycle for it would panic ERR_PERIOD_NOT_DUE. The coordinator approved the demonstration template 1 (same DAO, amount, cadence; start_at_ns = now) so the full second-cycle sequence and the replay-reuse control could be demonstrated in this session.

near-cli-rs 0.30.1 prints no transaction hash on failed sends; --teach-me verbose capture was added to the runner to recover hashes. Five onchain executions (four runA trap rejections and the runD claim success) remain uncaptured by hash; the consumed-nonce sequence (276384918000014..276384918000027) accounts for every transaction.

The task brief's expected panic strings (ERR_CYCLE_NOT_CLAIMED for claim_cycle, ERR_PROPOSAL_REPLAY for link_proposal) were not observed verbatim: claim_cycle on a SUBMITTED cycle asserts ERR_CYCLE_NOT_OPEN per the ABI (ERR_CYCLE_NOT_CLAIMED belongs to release_claim/submit_evidence), and the deployed build traps before the assert strings surface. Both controls still demonstrate the onchain rejection with no state change.
